article.title: Building Reliable Handover Documentation for Data Teams

paragraphs.en: A data team can produce excellent analysis and still create serious problems for its successors if important decisions remain undocumented. A new analyst may inherit a dashboard that works today but cannot explain where its numbers come from. Another developer may modify a calculation without knowing that an unusual exception was deliberately added to handle a business rule. Reliable handover documentation is therefore not simply a description of code. It is a map of decisions, dependencies, assumptions, and operational responsibilities that allows another person to understand and safely maintain the work. Without this map, the same questions return every time a team member changes.
paragraphs.zh: 資料團隊即使分析出色，若重要決策未記錄，仍會讓接手者陷入困境。新分析師可能接手能運作卻不知道數字來源的儀表板；開發者也可能不知某例外是刻意處理商業規則而改壞計算。交接文件不只是程式碼說明，更是決策、依賴、假設與責任的地圖。缺少它，人員變動就會重複同樣問題。
paragraphs.ja: 優れた分析でも判断の記録がなければ引き継ぎが難しくなります。数値の出所や特殊な業務ルールが分からないと安全に修正できません。文書はコード説明だけでなく判断と依存関係の地図です。

paragraphs.en: Begin with the purpose of the system. State which business decision it supports, who uses the output, and which questions it is not designed to answer. Then identify the authoritative data sources and explain how frequently they are updated. A table that looks similar to the official source may actually be a temporary extract. If two files contain different values, the documentation should make clear which one takes precedence. This source-of-truth principle prevents well-intentioned maintainers from creating competing versions of the same information. It also helps reviewers recognize when a result reflects stale data rather than a genuine change in customer behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 先寫系統目的、使用者與不適用問題，再列權威資料來源與更新頻率。看似正式的表格可能只是暫存匯出；兩檔數值不同時，文件應說明優先順序。單一真實來源原則可避免接手者建立互相競爭的版本，也能辨別過時資料與真正的客戶行為變化。
paragraphs.ja: まず目的、利用者、対象外の問いを示します。正式なデータ源と更新頻度、ファイルが食い違う場合の優先順位を記録します。古いデータと実際の変化も区別できます。

paragraphs.en: Next, document the data flow at a useful level of detail. Describe where records originate, which transformations occur, how identifiers are joined, and what the final output represents. Define the grain of each important dataset: one row per customer, transaction, account, or month. Include the timing rules used to prevent future information from entering historical predictions. A concise diagram can help, but it should be accompanied by text that explains exceptions. A diagram without definitions may look polished while leaving critical ambiguity unresolved. For important metrics, provide a small worked example that another analyst can calculate independently.
paragraphs.zh: 資料流程須記錄來源、轉換、串接鍵、輸出意義及每列粒度，例如客戶、交易或月份。也要寫明避免未來資訊流入歷史預測的時間規則。簡圖需搭配例外說明；重要指標最好有能獨立手算的小範例，避免漂亮圖表掩蓋歧義。
paragraphs.ja: データ源、変換、結合キー、粒度、予測時点を記録します。図だけでは例外を説明しきれないため、主要指標には手計算できる例も付けます。

paragraphs.en: Operational instructions should be reproducible. List the required environment, configuration steps, normal commands, expected outputs, and common failure messages. Explain how to run tests without changing production data. If the application writes to a shared source, describe the backup procedure, permission boundaries, and recovery steps. Include the checks that must pass before deployment. Avoid recording passwords or secret tokens in the document; instead, explain where authorized maintainers can obtain access through approved channels. Good documentation reduces risk without exposing sensitive credentials. A checklist should distinguish routine maintenance from actions that require explicit approval.
paragraphs.zh: 操作指引必須可重現：列出環境、設定、指令、預期輸出與錯誤；說明唯讀測試、備份、權限、復原及部署前檢查。不要在文件存密碼或權杖，而是說明授權取得途徑。清單應區分例行維護與需要明確核准的操作。
paragraphs.ja: 環境、設定、コマンド、期待結果、エラーを再現できる形で示します。バックアップや復旧方法も記載し、秘密情報は保存しません。承認が必要な操作を区別します。

paragraphs.en: A decision log is especially valuable when a project has undergone several redesigns. Record what changed, why the change was necessary, which alternatives were rejected, and whether any old behavior is intentionally unsupported. Without this context, a future developer may restore a retired feature because its code still exists. The log should distinguish current architecture from historical notes. A short, accurate explanation of the present system is more useful than hundreds of outdated pages. Archive obsolete material clearly rather than mixing it into active instructions. Whenever possible, connect a decision to the relevant test and the version where the behavior changed.
paragraphs.zh: 多次重構的專案需要決策紀錄：改了什麼、為何改、拒絕哪些方案、哪些舊行為已不支援。否則未來開發者可能恢復退役功能。應區分現行架構與歷史筆記，封存過時文件，並連結相關測試與變更版本。
paragraphs.ja: 変更理由、却下した代案、廃止機能を記録します。現行仕様と古い記録を区別し、関連する試験や変更版にもつなげます。

paragraphs.en: Finally, verify the handover by asking someone unfamiliar with the project to perform a realistic task. Can they locate the official source, explain a key metric, run a read-only test, and identify the safe deployment process? Their questions reveal missing information better than a review by the original author. Assign ownership for keeping the guide current, and update it whenever important behavior changes. Documentation is successful when it enables independent, safe action. Its value lies not in its length, but in how reliably another person can use it. Schedule periodic reviews so that an apparently complete guide does not quietly become misleading.
paragraphs.zh: 最後請不熟悉專案的人實際測試交接：找正式來源、解釋指標、執行唯讀測試及辨識安全部署。新人的疑問能揭露缺漏。指定文件負責人並定期審查，避免看似完整卻逐漸過時。文件價值在於讓他人獨立、安全地行動，而非篇幅。
paragraphs.ja: 初見の担当者に正式データ源の特定、指標の説明、読み取り専用試験、公開手順を試してもらいます。文書の責任者と定期見直しを設定します。
